title: Integrate route-level A/B experiment configs into policy engine (deterministic assignment + precedence)
creator: Jada Williams
description:
Goal
Implement policy evaluation changes required to support route-level A/B experiments in production routing. The policy engine must (a) recognize experiment configs attached to a route, (b) deterministically assign each eligible request to a variant (A/B/...), and (c) return a routing decision that is stable across retries/stream reconnects and compatible with existing rollout primitives.

Context
Console will allow customers to define experiments at the route level (e.g., /v1/chat/completions within a project). The data-plane (gateway/router) consults the policy engine to decide which upstream model/config to use. We already support canary rollouts, model pinning, and fallback routing. Experiments add a new policy type that splits traffic and requires deterministic bucketing.

Scope
1) Policy model + evaluation
- Add ExperimentPolicy (route-level) to policy engine schema.
- Implement evaluation step that:
  - checks eligibility rules (tenant/project/region, route match)
  - checks schedule state (draft/running/paused/stopped)
  - calculates deterministic assignment bucket -> variant
  - returns resolved upstream target (model_id + config profile) for that variant

2) Precedence rules (must be explicit and tested)
- Precedence order for a given request:
  1. Hard safety blocks (e.g., disabled route / kill-switch)
  2. Reliability fallback policies (only on error/timeout/capacity signals; not part of primary assignment)
  3. Route-level A/B experiment (if running + eligible)
  4. Canary rollout (if configured)
  5. Model pinning / default route target
- Important: experiments are measurement-oriented; they should not silently override an active fallback behavior. Fallbacks are applied after primary selection when triggered.

3) Deterministic assignment integration
- Use the shared assignment library (introduced in PR #18342) to compute buckets.
- Inputs should be a stable, privacy-safe key set (see ADR-0187):
  - tenant_id (required)
  - project_id (required)
  - route_id (required)
  - optional: end_user_id hash header (if present) OR api_key_id fallback
- Ensure variant stickiness is preserved across:
  - request retries
  - streaming reconnects (same request_id if provided)
- Return in the decision payload:
  - experiment_id
  - variant_id (e.g., "control", "treatment")
  - assignment_hash_version

4) Failure modes
- If experiment evaluation fails (bad config, missing variant target, assignment error):
  - do NOT fail open to an arbitrary variant
  - fall back to non-experiment route resolution and emit an internal error metric
- If policy engine is unavailable: existing gateway behavior applies (per current routing fallback).

Out of scope
- Multi-armed bandits / automated optimization
- Custom metrics routing
- Private (on-prem) gating logic beyond feature flag checks

References
- ADR-0187 deterministic assignment at route level
- ADR-0188 exposure logging + privacy (note: exposure emission is handled in gateway; this ticket only returns decision dimensions)
- GitHub PRs:
  - redwood/pr_18342_ab-testing-assignment-core
  - redwood/pr_18357_policy-engine-support-experiment-config (implements most of this ticket)

Open questions (tracked here until resolved)
- Should canary apply inside a variant target (e.g., variant selects a model family and then canary within it)? Current plan: No. Variant target is explicit and fully resolved to avoid conflating experiment measurement with rollout.
- How do we represent "paused" experiments in policy evaluation? Proposed: treat as not applicable; keep config but do not assign.

Owners
- Policy engine: Jordan Lee
- Routing review: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- PM sign-off on precedence semantics: Marissa Cole
acceptance_criteria:
Functional
- Policy engine supports ExperimentPolicy in config schema and can evaluate an experiment attached to a route.
- Deterministic assignment is stable for a given (experiment_id, sticky_key) across repeated requests.
- Decision response includes experiment_id + variant_id when an experiment applies.
- Eligibility rules respected (tenant/project/region/route) and schedule state respected (draft not applicable; running applicable; paused/stopped not applicable).
- On experiment evaluation error, routing falls back to standard non-experiment resolution and increments an internal error counter.
- Precedence rules enforced exactly as documented:
  - When experiment is running + eligible, it determines primary target ahead of canary/pinning.
  - Fallback routing is not used as a primary selector; it only triggers on error/timeout/capacity signals downstream.

Testing
- Unit tests cover:
  - bucket distribution correctness (incl. non-50/50 splits)
  - stickiness with different available keys (end_user_id present vs absent)
  - paused/stopped behavior
  - precedence interactions: experiment vs canary vs pinning
- Integration test (staging) validates:
  - consistent assignment across gateway retries for the same request_id
  - correct decision payload fields consumed by gateway

Review/Docs
- Security/privacy review completed for key inputs used for hashing (confirm no raw PII).
- Updated policy engine docs include new experiment policy type and precedence description.
perf_budget:
Policy evaluation overhead (incremental)
- Added per-request CPU cost in policy evaluation: p99 <= 250µs at 2k RPS per node (measured in staging perf harness).
- Memory allocations: no unbounded allocations per request; avoid per-request map growth; prefer precompiled allowlists.
- Config lookup: O(1) expected for route_id -> experiment mapping.
- Cardinality: do not add high-cardinality tags in policy-engine internal metrics beyond experiment_id (hashed or truncated if required by observability standards).
implementation_notes:
Implementation outline
- Extend policy schema:
  - ExperimentPolicy { experiment_id, state, start_at, end_at, route_id, eligibility, variants[], traffic_allocation, sticky_key_policy, hash_version }
  - Variant { variant_id, target_ref (model_id + config_profile_id) }
- In evaluator:
  - resolve applicable policies for route
  - check feature flag / entitlement (Hosted/Dedicated) before applying
  - if experiment applies, compute sticky_key (per ADR-0187) and call assignment lib
  - resolve variant target and return decision
- Precedence encoded as a single ordered evaluation pipeline (avoid scattered if/else across call sites).

Notes from review (routing)
- Mina: ensure variant target resolution happens before data-plane; gateway should not have to interpret experiment config beyond (experiment_id, variant_id, target).
- Ravi: do not mix experiment assignment with fallback selection; keep fallback logic separate and only downstream-triggered.

Related PR
- PR #18357 contains the bulk of the schema + evaluator changes. This ticket tracks remaining follow-ups: perf benchmarks + precedence tests + final reviews.
test_plan:
Unit
- evaluator_experiment_policy_applies_when_running_and_eligible
- evaluator_experiment_policy_not_applied_when_paused_or_stopped
- evaluator_experiment_precedence_over_canary
- evaluator_falls_back_on_invalid_variant_target
- assignment_stickiness_with_end_user_id
- assignment_stickiness_with_api_key_fallback

Integration (staging)
- Run gateway replay tool to issue 1k identical requests with same request_id and validate stable variant assignment.
- Run mixed traffic (requests with/without end_user_id header) and verify expected distribution within each cohort.

Perf
- Run policy-engine perf harness with 10 routes, 3 experiments, 2 variants each; measure incremental p50/p99 vs baseline build and attach results to this ticket before Done.
rollout_plan:
Rollout
- Behind feature flag: console.ab_experiments_enabled (control-plane gates config emission; policy engine also checks entitlement).
- Deploy policy engine changes to staging first; run integration + perf tests.
- Canary deploy to 5% of Hosted traffic in us-east for internal dogfood projects.
- Expand to 50% once guardrails (ENG-2845) dashboards show no regression; then 100%.

Rollback
- Disable feature flag to stop emitting/considering experiment policies (policy engine treats experiment configs as non-applicable).
- If severe regression in policy engine latency, roll back service deployment to previous build; no data migration required (schema is additive and ignored by older builds if not referenced by the gateway config snapshot).
comments: 2026-02-06 — Jordan Lee: Added initial ExperimentPolicy proto + evaluator stub on branch. Open question: best place to compute sticky_key—policy engine vs gateway. Leaning policy engine so decision payload is fully determined and can be logged consistently; gateway still emits exposure events.

2026-02-08 — Mina Haddad: +1 policy engine computing sticky_key/variant; gateway should remain dumb for experiment semantics. Please ensure request_id can influence stickiness on streaming reconnects (some clients reuse TCP but new HTTP req).

2026-02-10 — Ravi Menon: Precedence needs to be encoded once. We’ve been burned by canary vs pinning precedence diverging across services. Add tests that demonstrate: experiment primary selection happens before canary, but fallback still applies after primary target if the request errors.

2026-02-13 — Marissa Cole: Confirmed product semantics: experiments override canaries for primary selection. Canary is still allowed on the *non-experiment* path. Also, paused experiments should behave as if not configured (no assignment, no exposure).

2026-02-17 — Jordan Lee: PR #18357 up. Includes schema + precedence pipeline. Still need perf harness numbers and one more integration test for retry stickiness when end_user_id missing (api_key_id fallback).

2026-02-20 — Marcus Lin: Security note: ensure we never ingest raw end_user_id; only accept a pre-hashed header (documented) or hash server-side with a rotating salt that is not shared externally. Please document which mode we’re using in this release.

2026-02-21 — Jordan Lee: Addressed security feedback in PR: header must be 'x-rw-user-hash' (already hashed); otherwise we use api_key_id. Added evaluator metric 'experiment_assignment_error_total' (no high-card tags). Perf run scheduled Monday; leaving ticket In Review until results attached.
